questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Professional Reasons: 
- The supervisor and their expertise
- The research group and its environment
- The research topic and academic opportunities
- Exposure to new methods and techniques
- Expanding my knowledge into new boundaries

Other Reasons
- The weather and overall climate
- The culture and local lifestyle
- The student life and social opportunities
- How easy it is to meet new people and integrate

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Easy to meet people, an interesting project, and a good supervisor.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. My supervisor and the university were very helpful. I used the first week to get an introduction, enroll as a student, and take care of practical matters.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: From the University of Lisbon and my supervisor. I received emails about all the practical matters and scheduled a meeting to enroll as a student. Afterwards, I had a meeting with my supervisor to be introduced to the research group and traineeship.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy. There are multiple Facebook groups (both international and Danish) to find roommates.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I do not think it is possible to live on campus. The accommodation situation is very similar to Copenhagen.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was no help available, but there are many groups to find roommates and websites to search for apartments. Be aware of scammers.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were no problems.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Again, I received many emails from the university and scheduled a meeting to enroll.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Plenty.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did my master's thesis, so I had no classes. This was also a factor that made everything very easy.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not do it at the last minute when every new student is enrolling. Make sure to arrive in good time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very interesting and challenging. I learned a lot, and it was different from KU. Again, these were not classes. I got the impression that regular classes are much easier than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did my thesis.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I was part of a research group. We had mandatory meetings, discussion sessions, and weekly lectures we could attend. It was a great opportunity to meet academic professionals, get inspired, and learn how it works to be part of a research group.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Thesis

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I do not know. I did my thesis

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food and drinks is cheap.
If you want to go on trips with friends, it will cost more, but it's worth it. I would definitely recommend exploring the country and islands while being there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not experience any social opportunities at my host institution since I was doing a traineeship. I think there was a welcome week for international students, but it was not as good as at other universities. I met friends through my roommates and by going out.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not sure.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Be open and find good roommates in advance. People are very open and in the same situation as you. If you enjoy going out, you will meet a lot of nice people. Erasmus student life also offers multiple events, both during the day and at night, which are great, especially in the beginning. They have events throughout the month, so it's always a good way to meet new people or try new things.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Rent a van or car and drive around—it's very cheap and easy to do. Visit Porto and the small cities along the coast (e.g., Óbidos, Nazaré). 
Take a weekend trip to the Algarve and/or the Azores.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Look at erasmus life lisboa for events.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They are not as good in English, which can be a barrier.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and wine are amazing. People are better at going out for dinner and enjoying the night. The warmth and sunshine make everything even better.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: It's a perfect place to meet people and go out. It gives you a constant feeling of being on vacation.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Because I did my master's thesis, it is difficult for me to give advice on the host institution and how the classes are.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people and sun.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Differences in methods (during thesis) from KU.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: ENJOY

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
